To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existence of propaganda is inextricably bound to the existence of communication, and that propaganda is a set of techniques and processes which facilitate the propagation or suppression of ideas and actions, which can be used for both positive and negative purposes.
the use of propaganda is not limited to authoritarian regimes but is a tool of the political elite in liberal democratic states and is used by both the left and right.
digital media has changed the nature of propaganda. It has become more decentralized, more difficult to identify and more difficult to counter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way that propaganda has been transformed by the digital revolution and the way that the Internet is changing the way that propaganda is used.
the nature of the relationship between propaganda and digital media and the implications of this for democratic politics.
the nature of the relationship between propaganda and the digital environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
propaganda is a form of communication that is designed to influence attitudes and behaviours, and that it has existed since the dawn of human communication.
the digital age has not only created new forms of propaganda, it has also provided a means for counter-propaganda and self-corrective mechanisms.

propaganda is an evolving set of tools and mechanisms which are used in the propagation of ideas, and that these tools and mechanisms can be adapted to fit any context, whether vertical or horizontal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the internet has become a place where propaganda is used as a tool for political and social manipulation, and that the use of memes as propaganda has been successful in the case of Britain First.

the digital age has created a tyranny of ignorance, which is a product of a combination of propaganda techniques, the rise of echo chambers and the decline of the traditional gatekeepers of information, which is the media.
the Internet has become a battleground for ideas and beliefs, where the lines between propaganda and counter-propagation are increasingly blurred.
The main takeaway from our work is that

digital communication is an important and growing part of the propaganda landscape, but that the same mechanisms that allow for the spread of propaganda are also used by counter-propagandists and by those who seek to correct false information.
the nature of the internet as a communications medium has changed the nature of propaganda, but not its existence.
digital propaganda is a form of social control which relies on the tyranny of ignorance.
